analysis: Portfolio currently holds 3 quality positions (APP, MSFT, V) with ~$10,181 cash and $89,596 deployed. Portfolio heat is light at 1.80%, well below the 6% ceiling for 3-5 positions. All three existing positions are in reasonable shape — APP is the standout with +3.2%, MSFT is treading water near cost, and V is slightly ahead. The primary task now is evaluating whether to add a 4th position with available cash. Scanning the 30 candidates: the best setups combine (1) basing in the lower 40% of 52-week range, (2) confirmed uptrend or positive SMA50 slope, and (3) exceptional fundamental quality. MCO stands out — it is in a confirmed uptrend/basing phase, just 29% off its 52-week lows, sitting right at SMA50 with a positive slope, while operating one of the most durable moats in finance (credit ratings duopoly). ROE of 71%, op margin of 45.7%, and $2.3B FCF at fwd P/E 24 is attractive for a business this quality. Cash is constrained to ~$10K so position will be smaller than ideal, but the setup is asymmetric enough to justify deployment. UBER is the next-best candidate (23% range, uptrend basing, improving financials) but would require margin and is less dominant competitively than MCO. ADSK at 16% range and PEG 0.95 is intriguing but sits below SMA50 — no trend confirmation yet, better to wait. AMP and RJF both have negative SMA50 slopes, disfavoring entry now. Recommending 1 new trade (MCO) to bring portfolio to 4 positions. No forced trades beyond that — remaining candidates either lack trend confirmation or have negative slope momentum.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $446-450, ideally on a slight intraday pullback to or near the SMA50 (~$447). If market opens above $452, wait for a retest of SMA50 support before entry.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Moody's is a near-irreplaceable toll-road on global capital markets — issuers must get rated, creating recurring, high-margin revenue with minimal capital requirements. 71% ROE, 45.7% operating margin, and $2.3B in annual FCF speak to exceptional business quality. At fwd P/E ~24 with 8%+ revenue growth and a re-acceleration catalyst from capital market activity normalization, MCO is at a historically fair-to-cheap entry. TECHNICAL: Stock is basing at 29% of its 52-week range, sitting right at SMA50 with a slightly positive slope (+0.1%). The confirmed UPTREND with basing designation is exactly the Stage 1→2 transition preferred by this strategy. Notably, the stock is still 6.7% below SMA200, meaning there is meaningful room to recover before becoming extended. This is a patient, quality entry — not chasing momentum.
trades.exit_plan: Exit thesis-break if: (1) revenue growth decelerates below 5% for two consecutive quarters, (2) credit market volumes collapse due to a sustained risk-off environment, or (3) SMA50 slope turns sharply negative and price breaches $426 stop. Time stop: re-evaluate at 3 months if price has gone nowhere and SMA50 slope is flat or negative. Target trim at $520 (near prior 52-week high cluster); if thesis remains intact above $520, hold remaining shares toward LTCG.
